alpha_rule: light_max = shadow_max: the composite span between a full lit and a full shadowed slope, o*(a_l*(1 - v) + a_s*v) over a plate of value v at layer opacity o, is then o*a on every map style
credit: Elevation: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP), 1 arc-second DEM; resampled by this bundle (U.S. Geological Survey, U.S. public domain)
honesty: The shading is computed from ~150-185 m cell means: it shows ridges, valleys, terraces and levee belts at that scale, not street grades or buildings. Vertical exaggeration is a styling choice (AUTHORED) declared per region. Same-origin files; no tile service is contacted.
label: Relief shading: USGS 3DEP heights (RECORDED), shaded at build time (DERIVED)
method: Horn 3 x 3 gradient in metres per cell (east-west width x cos(latitude) per row), one sun at azimuth 315 deg, altitude 45 deg; facing the sun -> white, facing away -> black, flat -> transparent; a cell with no RECORDED height in its 3 x 3 window is transparent

bayarea.exaggeration_why: the Bay Area grid spans -63.5 to 1432 m; x1.5 keeps the flats readable without the ranges going black
bayarea.rows_resampled: nearest source row at equal Web Mercator steps between the north and south edges (1177 distinct source rows of 1181)
bayarea.what: the 9 San Francisco Bay Area counties of the Bay world, California

parishes.exaggeration_why: the parish grid spans -8.7 to 115.9 m over about 230 km; at x1 its levees, ridges and the Pleistocene terrace edge are below one grey level
parishes.rows_resampled: nearest source row at equal Web Mercator steps between the north and south edges (1240 distinct source rows of 1243)
parishes.what: the 13 parishes of the parish worlds, Louisiana
